Bacterial Blight: Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum. Remove and destroy infected debris, use certified acid-delinted seed, and avoid overhead irrigation because splashing spreads the bacteria.
Curl Virus: Cotton leaf curl virus, carried by whitefly. Control the whitefly rather than the virus, remove infected plants early, and prefer tolerant varieties.
Healthy Leaf: No disease or pest damage detected. Continue routine scouting and keep irrigation and nutrition steady.
Herbicide Growth Damage: Herbicide injury and not a pathogen. Review application rate, timing and sprayer calibration, then check for drift from neighbouring fields.
Leaf Hopper Jassids: Amrasca biguttula feeding damage. Inspect leaf undersides where nymphs sit. Treat at the local economic threshold and not on a fixed calendar.
Leaf Redding: A physiological response and not an infection. Common causes are nitrogen or magnesium shortage, water stress and cold nights. Take a soil test first.
Leaf Variegation: Patchy colouring, often a micronutrient shortage or a genetic trait. Check zinc, iron and magnesium, then watch whether the pattern spreads.
